properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency in the NFT app's web3 stack (root yarn.lock, alongside hash.js@1.1.7 for other ranges); hash.js implements the SHA-1/SHA-2 family. No direct call site in the app's own source — it is reached through ethers v5's internal hashing — but the lockfile entry is what ships these digests in the build. Changeable here by upgrading/removing the ethers dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 ships inside crypto-js 3.3.0 (the last 3.x release, 2016, unsupported), dragged in by eth-lightwallet@3.0.1 ← @0x/subproviders@4.1.2 ← web3-react@5.0.5 (deprecated legacy v5, declared as a runtime dependency of the frontend). Available in the shipped dependency tree; no application call site found in the repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js ships SHA-1 (plus MD5, AES, HMAC, etc.) in the build as a transitive dep. No direct call site in app source; the SHA-1 capability is present because the package is. Migrating means replacing the package that pulls crypto-js or pinning it out.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's RSA (plus X.509/TLS) implementation rides in via libp2p-crypto@0.21.2 ← the nft.storage/web3.storage IPFS stack. Available in the shipped library; no application call site found; no RSA key size configured anywhere.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pulled by ethereum-cryptography@2.2.1 (yarn.lock:7846), itself a dependency of web3-react@5.0.5 (yarn.lock:15890). Additional secp256k1 implementations ship via elliptic (ethers signing path) and @noble/secp256k1 via libp2p-crypto (yarn.lock:2379). The app's live signing path (Demo.tsx, hardhat) is ethers→elliptic; this noble copy is dependency-available, not app-called.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Both sites are real yarn.lock references to @noble/curves@1.4.2. Ed25519 ships via @noble/curves@1.4.2 (ethereum-cryptography@2.2.1 ← web3-react@5.0.5) and @noble/ed25519 via libp2p-crypto@0.21.2 (IPFS peer-ID stack). No application call site found; availability is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.4 is the secp256k1 signature implementation under @ethersproject/signing-key ← ethers 5.8.0 — the code path that executes the app's real signatures (Demo.tsx personal_sign request, hardhat deployment transactions). Other resolved copies: 6.6.1, 6.4.0, and the 2015-era 3.1.0 (eth-lightwallet). Highest-relevance dependency object in this shard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves 1.4.2 provides P-256 ECDSA/ECDH (as well as secp256k1 and friends) to the IPFS/web3.storage/ethers-adjacent packages in this tree. Same lockfile entry as the library object LIB-e9aa10c7 (which I also hold); no direct P-256 call site in the app's own code — the NFT app signs through the injected MetaMask wallet, not noble curves directly. Changeable here only by upgrading the packages that depend on it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the secp256k1 engine underneath ethers v5 in this project (the app's wallet-signing flow runs on it transitively). The lib's ECDH capability ships; the app's actual use of elliptic is ECDSA transaction/message signing, performed inside ethers. Replaceable only by upgrading the ethers/web3-react dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl resolves at three versions in this tree: 0.13.2 (eth-lightwallet ← web3-react@5.0.5), 0.14.3 (bcrypt-pbkdf, yarn.lock:5279), and ^1.0.0 (eth-sig-util@3.0.0, yarn.lock:7756). X25519 is the harvestable key-agreement class — any session negotiating with it is decryptable later. The repo's own code never calls it; it rides in the legacy wallet stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js's AES implementation ships in the build as a transitive dep (no direct app call site — no Node 'crypto' or crypto-js import anywhere in src/ or server/src). Note crypto-js AES defaults to ECB-ish unauthenticated modes when used naively; here nothing in this repo invokes it. Changeable by removing the package that pulls it in.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pbkdf2 browser polyfill is consumed by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (yarn.lock:7824) via the @ethereumjs/* toolchain; PBKDF2 derives Ethereum keystore (v3) encryption keys from passphrases. No application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.2.0 provides SHA-256 (and keccak256, which the Ethereum stack needs) as a transitive dep of the web3.storage/noble-curve packages. No direct call site in the app's own source; ships as library capability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.2.0 is pinned by ethereum-cryptography@1.2.0 (yarn.lock:7836). BLAKE3 also appears in the multiformats/IPFS CID path (blakejs via ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3). No application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 2.0.4 is the scrypt KDF used by ethers v5's keystore/JSON-wallet support in this tree. No direct call site in the app source (no keystore operations in src/ or scripts/); it ships as part of the ethers dependency chain. Parameters (N/r/p) are chosen by ethers at runtime, not fixed in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The SHA-3/Keccak family ships via @noble/hashes 1.2.0 (ethereum-cryptography@1.2.0); keccak256 is separately the EVM transaction/message hash via the keccak wasm package under ethers. No application call site found for the noble module.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ciphers 1.2.0 provides AEAD (salsa/chacha) and AES-GCM to the packages that pull it in this lockfile. No direct app call site; ships as library capability. Same lockfile entry as LIB-f169d8e1 (library facet) and ALG-c57b2423 (ChaCha20-Poly1305 facet) — one artifact, three inventory facets.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ChaCha20-Poly1305 capability of @noble/ciphers 1.2.0, shipped as a transitive dep. A+ rated and quantum-safe (256-bit); no action needed beyond inventory. No direct app call site — reached only through dependencies.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: A 2015-era build of libsodium's authenticated encryption rides in with eth-lightwallet@3.0.1 ← web3-react@5.0.5. No application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge brings a full X.509/PKI toolkit (certificate parsing/generation, RSA, PKCS) into the build as a transitive dep — no X.509 or PKI call site anywhere in the app or server source (no cert files are committed either). Its presence is the inventory fact: if any dependency ever needs TLS-cert handling, forge is what ships. Changeable by removing the package that pulls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.13.2 is a 2014-era release of the NaCl library (XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox, X25519 box, Ed25519 sign) shipped as a transitive dep. The 0.13.x line predates the audited 1.x rewrite. No direct call site in app source; it ships inside whatever package pins 0.13.2 in the lockfile. Recommend the owning dependency be identified and upgraded so 0.13.2 falls out of the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js 3.3.0 is the last 3.x release (2016), unsupported since; it ships MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, HMAC, AES, DES, RC4, Rabbit. Consumer: eth-lightwallet@3.0.1 ← @0x/subproviders@4.1.2 ← web3-react@5.0.5 (deprecated legacy v5, declared as a runtime dependency). Its presence is the posture fact: the frontend dependency tree carries a museum-grade crypto library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js resolves at 2.0.4 (this consumer) and 3.0.1 (ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3, yarn.lock:7827). Keystore/key-derivation class; no application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js is the streamable SHA-1/SHA-2 implementation from the browserify crypto stack, present as a transitive dep of the Ethereum toolchain (ethers v5 pulls it via its hashing deps). No direct call site in app source; ships as library capability. Same family as the hash.js sites (ALG-50e53f84) but a distinct package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Backs ethers 5.8.0's signing (Demo.tsx personal_sign, hardhat deploy transactions) via @ethersproject/signing-key. Other resolved copies: 6.6.1, 6.4.0, and the 2015-era 3.1.0 (eth-lightwallet). This is the object the app's eventual signature migration actually touches.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pinned by ethereum-cryptography@1.2.0; later @noble/hashes versions (1.4.0/1.7.x/1.8.0) also resolve for other consumers — @walletconnect/crypto@1.1.0 uses 1.7.0 for WalletConnect v1 session crypto. No application call site found for this copy.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js is elliptic's internal hash layer (SHA-256/512, HMAC) feeding the ECDSA keygen/signing path under ethers 5.8.0; 1.1.7 also resolves for other consumers. Rides with the ethers/elliptic signing stack that executes this app's real signatures.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The library facet of the same @noble/curves@1.4.2 lockfile entry as ALG-a6da3577 (P-256 facet, also mine, confirmed with cross-reference there). It is the curve engine for the noble stack in this tree (web3.storage/IPFS-adjacent packages); the app's own signing path goes through ethers v5/elliptic and the MetaMask wallet, not noble directly. Keep both facets: the LIB row records the shipped component, the ALG rows record which quantum-vulnerable primitives it makes available.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Browser-compat PBKDF2 used by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 and keystore tooling in the @ethereumjs/* stack. No application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The library facet of the @noble/ciphers@1.2.0 lockfile entry (same artifact as ALG-f61ec50f AES-GCM and ALG-c57b2423 ChaCha20-Poly1305, both confirmed). Ships as a transitive dep; no direct call site in this repo's own code. Keeping library + algorithm facets lets the CBOM record both the component and the primitives it provides.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pulled by libp2p-crypto@0.21.2 (yarn.lock:10973) via the nft.storage/web3.storage IPFS stack. 1.3.1 is the post-CVE-2022-24717/24771-fix line. Available in the shipped library; no application call site found.
